I LOVE AND HATE THIS GAME  AT THE SAME TIME.

SE used to be my favourite game of all times but since it is plagued by blatant cheaters using off-map hacks and auto aim bots, the game is no longer enjoyable. Reporting this cheaters makes no difference at all, they won't get banned. Such a shame because this game has a lot of potential.

EDIT: the cheaters issue has been resolved and I give developers credit for it.

However, there is something that bothers me a lot. In online mode, there is a bunch of 5 year old kids with no skills whatsoever, camping placidly in the same bush they respawned and when they get massacred they cowardly and anonymously vote to kick or cry cheater. After this point, the game turns into a spiral of everyone voting each other that I have found to be beyond pathetic. 

------  I SPEND WAY TOO MUCH TIME VOTING TO KICK THOSE WHO WANT TO KICK ME  ------

By allowing to vote anonymously you are giving useless noobs the ability to bully and harass well experienced players with actual skills and combat strategy.  

For this I request developers to reveal the name of voters so they can be dealt with.

Axis invasion is a great idea but the invaded sniper has an unfair advantage over the invader since he has the ability to sense the direction of the invader. Come on, really? All they do is fill the map with mines and camp for an hour, then kill the invader once he is in range. There is no game. Invasion is only fun in authentic mode without this sensorial BS.

Developers need to remove this nonsense for next versions of SE so invaders can hunt the invaded sniper and use real life tactics to get him by surprise.

To summarize: 

Best videogame ever made but I am not enjoying it.
good graphics and great game play
Could be better, nothing new really.

[h1]Sniper Elite Resistance: A Step Backward for the Series[/h1]

I’ve been a dedicated fan of the [i]Sniper Elite[/i] series since the very beginning, and to me, the franchise peaked with the third and fourth installments. While the fifth game was acceptable, it was clear that developer Rebellion's practices to monetize their games were in full swing. Because of this, even when a new game in the series is decent, I find it difficult to give it a good rating. It seems the developers don't understand that these scummy monetization practices will eventually drive away the most loyal fans, leaving them with no one.

[h2]Gameplay and Mechanics[/h2]

Frankly, very little has changed in [b]Sniper Elite Resistance[/b] from the fifth game, and what has changed often feels like a step backward. The large, open-world maps that have defined the series since [b]Sniper Elite 4[/b] make a return, which is a good thing in theory. However, the maps feel far too large and empty for the number of enemies present. It seems like enemy patrols roam without any cohesion, making them feel like a scattered, disorganized mess rather than a tactical military unit. This lack of enemy density means you spend more time running between mundane objectives than you do engaging in tactical combat. The days of setting intricate traps and outmaneuvering patrols are gone because there simply aren't enough enemies to make it worthwhile. You can also easily aggro the entire map and pick off enemies as they poorly attempt to find you. They'll just keep coming until only the enemies who are rooted in place are left. It should feel like a shooting gallery, but it even fails to hit that mark because it's just watching enemies run around the map and take cover in the same five spots.

I've played on Authentic difficulty since [b]Sniper Elite 3[/b] and spent countless hours mastering the language of muzzle velocity, windage, and gravity. Unfortunately, it feels like the series has put less and less emphasis on this mode with each new installment. [b]Sniper Elite Resistance[/b] takes this a step further; I've been able to complete entire maps using just a Welrod and a Thompson. For the most part, the maps are completely devoid of wind, even on Authentic, making it feel more like a basic hitscan shooter than a true sniper simulation.

Another major issue is the sheer abundance of ammo and tools scattered across the map. You can find enough ammunition to take on a small army, let alone the hundred or so enemies on a given map. Generators, which used to be a rare and valuable way to mask your shots, are now plentiful. On the third map alone, I found six generators all within close proximity. This laziness in item placement shows a lack of thoughtful design. Ammo carts appear in nonsensical locations, like by a lone shrub hundreds of feet from any enemy patrol. The entire experience feels empty, lacking challenge, and poorly designed.

[h2]Story and Setting[/h2]

Like other [b]Sniper Elite[/b] games, the story is largely a backdrop for the action, but I found myself so annoyed with the main character, Harry, that I turned off all in-game voices and relied solely on subtitles. While I tried switching to Karl, I was disappointed to find he still spouts his same tired, overly-obvious lines, like "Tall grass, good for hiding" and "SMG, in case things get hectic." These lines feel like they were written for infants and serve as nothing but an annoying distraction. Harry, however, is on another level, sounding like a bargain-bin Jason Statham. With his punchable face and horrible voice, I ended up skipping every cutscene and ignoring the story entirely.

[h2]Graphics and Sound[/h2]

Visually, [b]Sniper Elite Resistance[/b] looks like a game from 2010. There are times when it looks worse than games like [i]Halo: Reach[/i], especially the jagged, low-detail mountains in the background. It's clear that Rebellion is still using the same engine it's been beating to death since [i]Aliens vs. Predator[/i]. Anti-aliasing still doesn't work, and like the previous games, I had to install a third-party tool like ReShade to get any modern visual effects. The game has severe screen tearing even with G-Sync enabled on high-end hardware. Many of the assets, including guns, enemy models, and animations, appear to be copy-pasted directly from [b]Sniper Elite 4[/b] and [b]5[/b]. The sound is acceptable, but I can't speak to the music, as I turned that off along with the voice acting.

[h2]Pros and Cons[/h2]

[b]Pros:[/b]

    The fundamental sniping and stealth mechanics are still present, though watered down

    It still feels like a [b]Sniper Elite[/b] game

[b]Cons:[/b]

    Game is far too easy, even on the hardest difficulty

    Mind-numbing story and terrible voice acting

    Outdated graphics and technical issues

    Repetitive and uninspired mission design

    Maps feel empty due to low enemy count

    The inclusion of Denuvo anti-tamper, which causes occasional performance hitches

    Scummy monetization practices for legacy content

[h2]Conclusion[/h2]

[b]Sniper Elite Resistance[/b] is a disappointing entry in a series that I once loved. It feels like a tired and uninspired sequel, relying on the same old formula without adding anything new or interesting. The game's core mechanics, which have been a highlight of the series, are undermined by lazy design choices and a lack of polish. This is all compounded by Rebellion's business practices. It’s hard to justify their approach when they are charging $4-5 for two guns—the Mosin and the 1911—that have been staples in every previous [b]Sniper Elite[/b] game. These aren’t even included in the season pass, forcing players to pay extra on top of their full-priced game and season pass purchase. This makes the company feel more like an asset flip operation than a true developer. I would only recommend this to the most die-hard fans of the series, and even then, I'd suggest waiting for a significant sale.

Resistance is an good game.  I've played all of the SE games thus far and I feel this version was sub-par to SE4 which I personally enjoyed much better than all of the previous games and SE Resistance. The game something new and fresh in my opinion. The AI has become very predictable and the game mechanics are wearing very thin on me at this juncture. I enjoyed the game, but I shelved it for the time being. I don't plan to re-play it again.

Generally speaking, Sniper Elite games are amazing. The vibes and atmosphere are very good.
Sniper Elite Resistance is something brilliant with good AI, nature, weapons, etc...
The Axis Invasion mode is so stunning and fun to play, especially for patient people xD.
The only thing I didn't like about this version is the maps and map designs. They are playable at least, but they are not designed for sniping. They were designed for close-range stealth kills such as by pistol and knife. In some maps you need to create a loud sound by manipulating with some objects likes generators or cars so you can snipe, and this is annoying. 

Recommend this game? Yes, for sure.
